quotes.text: Your data flow can look fine today and still be hanging by a thread. Most people assume that if it refreshes without error, it's done.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Challenges the common assumption that a successful refresh means a dataflow is finished.

quotes.text: Every complex transform should be a named function with a clear input output signature and a single parameter back. If you can't explain it in one sentence, split it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concrete, easy-to-apply rule for modular dataflow design.

quotes.text: In fabric, Delta isn't optional, it's the difference between governed storage and a heap of csvs disguised as a platform.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear position on why Delta Lake is the foundation of a governed lakehouse.

quotes.text: Piling on more capacity won't fix poor design here. You can burn through budget on bigger machines, but if you're still slicing data into toothpick partitions and reloading everything nightly, performance will sink.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why design, not capacity, drives dataflow performance.

quotes.text: Modularize your transformations into functions, parameterize every environmental value, and keep shared logic centralized. When reuse must cross workspaces, do this and dataflow stop being disposable hacks and start becoming durable assets.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the recipe for reusable dataflows.

takeaways: A dataflow that refreshes today is not necessarily reusable; schema drift, hardcoded values and spaghetti logic make it fragile.
Modular Power Query M functions and centralized parameters turn one-off dataflows into reusable building blocks, while heavy shared logic belongs in the lakehouse or notebooks.
Landing data in Delta Lake and applying sensible partitioning and incremental refresh keep Fabric pipelines trustworthy, auditable and fast.
hook: Your Fabric dataflow refreshed this morning, but will it survive the next schema change? This episode is for data engineers and Fabric admins tired of fragile, hardcoded pipelines. Learn how modular design, parameters, Delta Lake, partitioning and incremental refresh turn disposable dataflows into durable assets.
